title: paged KV cache: block allocator reuse + pinning optimizations
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: reduce KV cache fragmentation and allocator churn in the paged KV cache, improve tail latency and memory stability for long-running model serving processes. This PR implements allocator reuse for freed blocks, introduces pinning semantics to prevent premature eviction of recently used KV blocks during active sequences, and adds a TTL-based eviction pass for low-pressure scenarios. Changes include a freelist-backed block allocator with size class buckets, reuse heuristics that prefer recently-freed blocks to reduce GPU memory churn, per-block pin counters to avoid eviction during active use, and a TTL sweep that opportunistically consolidates small free fragments. Also adds metrics, unit and integration tests, and a micro-benchmark harness. See Linear ENG-4823 and ENG-5011 for evaluation requests. Checklist: - [x] implement allocator reuse buckets - [x] add block pin/unpin APIs and usages in runtime scheduler - [x] TTL sweep and consolidation - [x] metrics + dashboards - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] benchmarks and perf numbers attached. Impact: expected latency p95 reduction under KV-heavy workloads, lower OOM rate for long-lived processes, and reduced allocator-induced stalls. Backwards compatibility: public APIs unchanged, internal behavior improved. Rollout: feature behind runtime flag paged_kv_builder.reuse_pinning_enabled (false by default) for staged rollout.

review_comments: Marco Nguyen: Nice work overall. Two requests: 1) please add a metric for allocator fragmentation ratio exposed to Console so we can track regressions, 2) make the TTL sweep non-blocking on the main allocation path.
Aisha Patel: Added fragmentation_ratio gauge and moved TTL sweep to background worker with cooperative yields. See commit aisha/paged-kv: TTL sweep that consolidates adjacent free blocks.
Liam O'Connor: There's a race in pin/unpin when blocks are freed concurrently with a TTL sweep. Can we add a generation check or acquire the pin lock in the sweep?
Aisha Patel: Reworked pin counters to be atomic u32 and added a generation stamp checked by the sweep. Added a unit test reproducing the race and verified fix in CI.
Sofia Ramirez: Benchmarks look promising but please include p50/p95/p99 numbers and memory consumption over time for the release notes.
Aisha Patel: Bench harness extended and results attached below. p95 tail latency improves ~12% for KV-heavy chat workloads; resident GPU memory growth reduced by ~18% across 24h simulated sessions.
ci_checks: e2e: nightly canary run (flaky on GPU infra) - rerun green
benchmark_summary: Setup: 8x A100, 32-token average prefix, mixed chat workload with KV reuse patterns
Throughput: +6% tokens/sec at 99%ile throughput under steady state when reuse enabled
Latency: p95 token latency reduced by ~12% on KV-bound sequences, p99 reduced ~8%
Memory: resident GPU memory growth over 24h reduced by ~18% in long-lived sessions
Allocation churn: allocator calls reduced by ~45% in benchmark trace due to reuse heuristics
CPU: background TTL sweep accounted for <1.5% CPU on serving processes in production-like load
release_notes: paged KV cache: improved allocator reuse and pinning to reduce fragmentation and tail latency
Added background TTL sweep to opportunistically consolidate free blocks
Feature gated behind paged_kv_builder.reuse_pinning_enabled (disabled by default); enable incrementally
summary: Implements block allocator reuse, pin/unpin semantics, and a TTL sweep to reduce fragmentation and allocator churn in the paged KV cache. Adds metrics, tests, docs, and benchmarks. Merged to main via squash.
notes_for_ops: Enable behind flag and monitor kv_allocator_fragmentation_ratio and kv_ttl_sweep_runs. If p95 regressions observed, disable reuse_pinning flag and open ENG-5011 for follow-up.
